To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the red blood cells are a suitable model for the evaluation of mercurial chalating agents.

(i) the red blood cells are an efficient model for the in vitro studies of the mercuric chelation by thiols; (ii) DMSA is the most effective chelant for methyl mercury; and (iii) Thiola and MSA are less effective than DMC, whereas DDC is almost ineffective.
DMSA was a better mercuric ion chelator than other thiols in both red blood cells and in hepatocytes, whereas BAL and DDC were considerably less effective in the latter cell system.
